title: The rank of apparition characterization
content: For fixed $k\ge1$, the indices $n$ where $k\mid F_n$ are exactly the multiples of a single index $\alpha(k)$, the rank of apparition (Fibonacci entry point). This gives $k\mid F_n\iff\alpha(k)\mid n$, generalising the modulus-specific corollaries $2\mid F_n\iff3\mid n$ etc. of the parent, and dual to $F_m\mid F_n\iff m\mid n$. Mathlib has the strong-divisibility backbone `fib_gcd`/`fib_dvd` but nothing on the rank of apparition; this file supplies both the minimality characterisation and existence of $\alpha(k)$.
mathContext: $k\mid F_n\iff\alpha(k)\mid n$, with $\alpha(k)$ the least positive index of divisibility.

title: dvd_fib_iff_of_least: the finiteness-free core
content: If $a$ is any least positive index with $k\mid F_a$, then $k\mid F_n\iff a\mid n$ — with no finiteness hypothesis. Forward: $k\mid F_a$ and $k\mid F_n$ give $k\mid\gcd(F_a,F_n)=F_{\gcd(a,n)}$ (`Nat.fib_gcd` + `Nat.dvd_gcd`); since $\gcd(a,n)>0$, minimality forces $a\le\gcd(a,n)$, while `gcd_dvd_left` gives $\gcd(a,n)\le a$, so $\gcd(a,n)=a$ and $a\mid n$. Converse: `Nat.fib_dvd` gives $F_a\mid F_n$, and $k\mid F_a$ transports. This isolates the algebra from the existence question.
mathContext: least positive $a$ with $k\mid F_a$ $\Rightarrow$ $(k\mid F_n\iff a\mid n)$.

title: The bijective Fibonacci shift and the pair orbit
content: The engine of the existence proof. The shift $(a,b)\mapsto(b,a+b)$ is packaged as an `Equiv` of $(\mathbb{Z}/k)^2$ with explicit inverse $(a,b)\mapsto(b-a,a)$ — bijectivity is what makes the pair sequence *purely* periodic. `shift_fibPair` proves one step of `fibPair k n = (F_n,F_{n+1})\bmod k$ equals one application of the shift (via `fib_add_two`), and `fibPair_eq_iterate` shows the sequence is the shift orbit $\text{shift}^n(0,1)$ by induction.

title: exists_pos_dvd_fib: existence via pigeonhole
content: Every $k\ge1$ divides some positive-index Fibonacci number. `exists_pos_dvd_of_pair_eq` takes a collision $p_i=p_j$ ($i<j$) and, using injectivity of $\text{shift}^i$, cancels the common prefix to get $p_0=p_{j-i}$; reading the first coordinate gives $F_{j-i}\equiv F_0=0\pmod k$, i.e. $k\mid F_{j-i}$ with $j-i>0$. `exists_pos_dvd_fib` produces the collision from `Finite.exists_ne_map_eq_of_infinite` — pigeonhole of infinite ℕ into the finite square $(\mathbb{Z}/k)^2$.
mathContext: $k\ge1\Rightarrow\exists n>0,\ k\mid F_n$, via a repeat in $(\mathbb{Z}/k)^2$.

title: entryPoint and the main characterization
content: With existence a theorem, `entryPoint k := Nat.find (exists_pos_dvd_fib k)` is a total, computable definition, and `Nat.find`'s API supplies `entryPoint_pos`, `dvd_fib_entryPoint`, and minimality `entryPoint_le`. The main theorem `dvd_fib_iff_entryPoint_dvd` is then just `dvd_fib_iff_of_least` instantiated at `entryPoint k`, giving the unconditional $k\mid F_n\iff\alpha(k)\mid n$ for all $k\ge1$.

title: Concrete entry points
content: Three worked examples applying `dvd_fib_iff_of_least` directly (so no `Nat.find` evaluation): $\alpha(2)=3$ ($2\mid F_n\iff3\mid n$, since $F_3=2$), $\alpha(3)=4$ ($F_4=3$), and $\alpha(5)=5$ ($F_5=5$, the fixed point where entry point equals modulus). Each discharges the minimal-witness obligation by `decide` on the small Fibonacci numerals $F_1,\dots,F_5$ and `omega` on the index case-split.
